newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to reveal state rescue for GAN insurer.
newsitem.headline: France to reveal state rescue for GAN insurer.

text.p: The French government was poised to reveal plans for another big rescue package in the financial sector on Thursday, for loss-making, state-controlled insurance Groupe des Assurances Nationale (GAN).

Share trading in GAN and its troubled UIC property arm was suspended on the Paris stock exchange on Thursday as the board prepared to meet and finance minister Jean Arthuis announced he would hold a news conference on the company at 1630 GMT.

Although the scale of the problem pales beside the repeated state rescues of state bank Credit Lyonnais, analysts say the cost of a capital injection and hefty provisions to cover property business losses, mainly at its UIC arm, could hit 20 billion francs ($3.5 billion).
About 20 percent of GAN's shares are traded on the stock exchange.

While the ministry said no more than that Arthuis would hold a news conference, sources close to the case said that he would reveal the scale of the problem, the causes and the cost of sorting it out.
No one was immediately available for comment at GAN.
The government wants to privatise GAN but the whole project has been complicated by the failure of a tender last year to first sell off GAN banking unit Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC).

It still plans to privatise CIC, a profitable group of 13 regional banks, but cancelled an original tender for a trade sale in November after receiving just two offers, of which only one -- from BNP bank -- was judged eligible by France's independent Privatisation Commission.

The European Commission, which vets state aid to industry in the European Union, approved a state injection of 2.9 billion francs into GAN last year and said recently that any new aid would require fresh investigation.
GAN's shares, which many analysts have now relegated to the status of a speculative stock, last traded at 123.0 francs.

The company issued a statement on February 14 to counter a recent rise in its stock price fuelled by market speculation that it could be a bid target in financial sector consolidation following the giant merger of insurers Axa and UAP.
Shares plunged after the company said the recent rise was not justified by its financial situation.
GAN made a loss of 1.79 billion francs in 1995 after a loss of 5.34 billion francs the previous year, with provisions for troubles at its UIC property financing unit eating into the accounts.
UIC announced a first-half loss of 711 million francs and said the property market, which collapsed in France in the early 1990s, hitting many banks and insurers, remained depressed.
As a result the GAN group itself reported a loss of nearly a billion francs in the first half of the year.

While the company is not due to formally sign off its 1996 accounts until April, analysts and French newspapers have been speculating that a recent audit could lead to a clean-up of the accounts and a very hefty loss for 1996.

The government package is expected to cover a capital injection, provisioning and, perhaps, a promise of further money to cover losses on future property sale losses as the group attempts to sort out UIC on a more permanent basis.
